Posted April 23, 2003
See
 International Update: Preview of NORML Conference Report On Developments In Cannabis Policies Around the World By Richard Cowan.
(MarijuanaNews note: Yesterday, the Volkskrant, a mass circulation Dutch paper, carried the article below. It was sent to Mapinc.org by my friend Ambassador Jan van der Tas, a retired Dutch diplomat, who is very active in the anti-prohibitionist movement.
See
 Leading Dutch Anti-Prohibitionists Say, The Quality Of The Drugs-Debate Is Abominable.
and
 We Are Winning! The Dutch Government Shows More Confidence that Things Are Going Our Way in Europe.

The Dutch parliament is still in the process of trying to form a coalition government after the elections in January. Dutch parliaments are based on proportional representation, with the result that no single party comes close to getting a majority. Holland is a very democratic country, but its politics can be a bit opaque because so much depends on negotiations between the leaders of the various groups.

First, the Dutch coffee shop system is indeed safe.
See
 Dutch Government Reconfirms Coffee Shop Policy. Drops Any Mention of Closing Border Shops. The Justice Minister Is Educating the Prime Minister.

But the good news is even better than this indicates, and in a bit of great irony we may have Bush and Rumsfeld to thank for it, at least in part, along with Jacque Chirac. And this isn't the first time that Chirac has made a fool of himself.
From 1998 see
 Was The Week That -- Wasn't What the Prohibitionists Planned;
The UN " Drug " Summit Farce

The European Union is in the process of adding ten new members, all of which, with the exception of Poland, are relatively small countries that are worried about EU domination by Germany and France.

Even though they had serious misgivings about the Iraq war, the former Soviet satellite countries look to the US for protection, not the French or Germans, for obvious historical and military reasons. But within the EU context they look to The Netherlands, as the most successful and important of the small countries, for leadership against the French and Germans. Chirac reinforced this tendency when he scolded the prospective new members for siding with the Americans over the Iraq war.
See
 Unintended Consequences: How The Iraq War Has Changed the Global Climate for Cannabis Prohibition. Analysis by Richard Cowan

Drugs policy had nothing to do with any of this, but most of the Europeans, including the Germans, now recognize that the Dutch are doing a better job of handling it than any other EU country. [Switzerland is not in the EU, but its policies are similar to the Dutch.]
See
 We Are Winning! Switzerland to Surpass the Dutch and Allow Not Only Use and Sales But Also Cultivation. Major Impact On Germany and the Rest of Europe.

Only the French and the Swedes share the DEAland hard line approach. They are the prohibitionist menage a trois, taking strange bedfellows to the absurd extreme.

Last June, at meeting of EU Justice Ministers, Sweden and France objected to the Netherlands being exempted from new EU minimum sentences for drug dealing, so there was no common decision. The Dutch stood up for their system.
See
The Accelerating Disintegration of Marijuana Prohibition in Europe. If the Tories Are all about sex, drugs and rock'n'roll, Where Can the Left Go? Embarrassment for Swedes. Dutch PM for Dinner.

DEAland can't do much to pressure the Dutch. First, the Dutch bought off Washington by letting DEAland use its airbases in the Antilles for Plan Colombia and the Dutch were relatively supportive of the Bush in the Iraq war. Former Drug Czar McCaffrey destroyed what little credibility DEAland had with the Dutch.
See
Drug Czar Uses Foreign Affairs Magazine Article For Anti-Dutch Propaganda,
Elevating The Lying To Official Status. Analysis By Richard Cowan
and links

The UK is the odd man out on this, as is often the case in the EU. The Blair government was annoyed that the UN narks objected to the rescheduling of cannabis, claiming that it would send the wrong message to African dictators. Really!
See
UN Nark's Speech To Swedish Prohibitionists May Cause Permanent Brain Damage. Illogic, Ignorance and Lying, Especially About the Dutch, Of Course.

Clearly Europe continues to move toward accepting the Dutch model, but it will take time, so we should not expect dramatic changes in the near term.)

April 22, 2003
(Translators Note: The Second Chamber is the Dutch House of Commons. Currently a new coalition cabinet is being formed. Translation from Dutch by Harry Bego. Political Party names with a notation of " HB " inserted for clarification.)

Chamber For Legalisation Of Soft Drugs

THE HAGUE - A large majority of the Second Chamber supports the plea of the Maastricht Court president Lampe for legalisation of soft drugs. Only CDA (Christian Democrats - HB ) wants to keep marijuana and hash under criminal law to prevent the Netherlands from being flooded by drug tourists.

Only CDA wants to keep hash under criminal law. CDA advocates strict adherence to current tolerance policy. " We must tune our drug policy with neighbouring countries. Otherwise we only import more drugs misery ", CDA MP Van Haersma Buma says. VVD (liberal conservatives - HB ) MP Griffith states that the opinions of Judge Lampe are in full agreement with the opinions of her party. " Drugs are a part of our society, you have to live with that. "

Court president (Judge) Lampe last weekend criticised the clogging of the judicial system by the large amount of drugs cases. Other serious crimes remain unsanctioned or their trials are greatly delayed. Lampe thinks that legalisation of drugs, starting with soft drugs, can help.
(MarijuanaNews note: Cannabis growers are sometimes prosecuted. Also, selling other drugs remains illegal. Drugs are not legal in The Netherlands, contrary to popular misconceptions, so they have many of the problems associated with the Drug War.)

PvdA, VVD, SP, LPF, GroenLinks and D66 support the plea by Lampe with respect to marijuana and hash.

" Wise words from a man who knows ", PvdA (Labour party - HB ) MP Albayrak says. Two years ago a proposal by PvdA to legalise soft drugs achieved a minute majority.
See
Dutch Parliament Surprises Its Own Government -- Votes to " Legalize " Cultivation of Marijuana By One Vote.

" But the government refused to do anything with it. We call upon the new cabinet-to-be to take this almost Chamber-wide desire seriously ".

Intended CDA coalition partner VVD shares that opinion. Spokesperson Griffith however thinks that as many allies as possible must be found in Europe and the rest of the world. United Nations treaties at the moment hinder the depenalisation of sale, trade and production of soft drugs.
See
Swiss Government Says Going Dutch Does NOT Violate Treaties. Implications for Other Countries, Especially Canada and UK. Plus Full Text of UN Nark Press Release.

The third candidate government party, D66 (liberal democrats - HB ), has been in favor of the legalisation of soft drugs for years. " In that way one cuts organised crime off ", faction leader and former Judge Dittrich says. Moreover, by legalising production, state control over THC-content, the active ingredient in marijuana, is enabled. Dittrich: " And that is necessary too. Soft drugs are becoming ever stronger ".
(MarijuanaNews note: Yes and no. First, this statement shows that even anti-prohibitionists can fall for the prohibitionist party line. Reported average THC levels in Dutch cannabis has been increasing, but that does not make it more dangerous, but people need to know what they are smoking.)
See
 Potent Pot Myth Undermined By Report From The Ultimate Authority. Cited By Swedish Prohibitionist Who Don't Seem To Understand. As Usual.
and from 1998, somewhat out of date data
The Prohibitionists In Stockholm Reveal The Shocking Truth
About The Potency Of Dutch Marijuana

LPF (List Pim Fortuyn - HB ) prefers to hand over the sale of soft drugs to pharmacists. " We don't want to place it next to the sweets in the supermarket. Otherwise you'll be causing all young people to use drugs ", LPF MP Eerdmans thinks.
(MarijuanaNews note: Another anti-prohibitionist that doesn't understand.)
